facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic, prepared in April 2016, states that 'currently' 38 of the 65 offices of the Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration have access to the NPRS; it adds that since 2012 every office with access must capture new birth and death records in the system, but gives no count of offices doing so.

The diagnostic describes the NPRS at its November 2015 fieldwork as an integrated, web-based civil registration system in which offices with access capture new birth and death records, regional offices having captured death records live since 2013, with birth and death certificates issued locally and on the spot.

The diagnostic states that in November 2015 the ministry held in the NPRS digital records of 280,000 births and 460,000 deaths, and gives from the NPRS 92,975 birth registrations in 2015, of which 18,982 were within 30 days of birth.

The diagnostic states that the Department of Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration uses and runs the NPRS, which the Office of the Prime Minister developed on the basis of the old ID system and backs up.

The diagnostic states that a strategic action plan for civil registration and vital statistics for 2015-2021 was approved by the authorities in February 2015, after the 2014 assessment, one recommendation of which was a new birth application form for collecting data from the NPRS; it adds that the plan needs clearer policy and financial support.

systems.platform: integrated web-based system developed by the Office of the Prime Minister on the basis of the old ID system
systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration, Department of Civil Registration
systems.tiers: 38 of 65 ministry offices have access; regional and sub-regional offices and offices in 22 of 35 hospitals register births; organised around the unique identity number, linking children to parents' records since 2011

systems.platform: M-files for birth records, then the NPRS for historical death and marriage records
systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration, with Document Warehouse under contract
systems.tiers: began February 2010; about 2.7 million birth records captured in M-files (4.3 million stored), 379,447 historical death records and 130,184 marriage records in the NPRS; digitalisation of all existing records stated complete by 31 May 2016

systems.platform: a Chinese AFIS, as the report calls it
systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration
systems.tiers: central; fingerprints taken in ink on paper forms

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration; card production and maintenance contracted out
systems.tiers: live capture of signature and picture at regional offices, scanning and card printing at head office; 20 of 65 offices do ID registrations

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration
systems.tiers: regional offices and head office; tested, pilot planned for April-May 2016

systems.system: Secure online portal for verifying birth, marriage and death certificates
systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration
systems.tiers: being established, for approved users such as insurers and pension funds

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration
systems.tiers: areas far from a registration office; the teams have had difficulty reaching the NPRS to verify identities

systems.system: Government wide area network and VSAT links
systems.owner: Office of the Prime Minister, with Telecom Namibia
systems.tiers: operational in Windhoek, regional hubs by November 2015; ministry offices to be connected case by case; ministry data centre link of 512 kb/s to 1 Mb/s, unstable

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration and Electoral Commission of Namibia
